newsitem.title: UK: Lib Dems propose plan to downsize UK car fleet.
newsitem.headline: Lib Dems propose plan to downsize UK car fleet.

text.p: The Liberal Democrats on Tuesday announced a plan to persuade Britons to drive smaller cars in what the party said would be the first of a series of environmental initiatives in their election campaign.

They said vehicle excise duty should be slashed to 10 stg a year from 145 stg for vehicles of up to 1600 cc, with the money lost to the treasury being made up by a four pence a litre increase in petrol duty.
"This would put money into the pockets of the great majority of motorists," said environment spokesman Matthew Taylor.
"It would hit those who continue to use gas guzzlers to cover large distances, but we want to give them a financial incentive to change."

Taylor said an average motorist driving a small car would be 92 stg a year better off if the policy were brought in, while the driver of a typical 3,500 cc car doing 20,000 miles a year would pay an extra 185 stg a year in petrol duty.

Party leader Paddy Ashdown -- who admitted that one of the two cars in his family was well above the 1600 cc ceiling -- said he feared the environment would receive scant attention from Labour and the Conservatives during the campaign.
"I greatly fear that the environment, one of the greatest issues facing mankind as a whole, will be left out completely. We Liberal Democrats are determined that it should not be," he said.

Ashdown said the party's election manifesto would include a plan for a major programme of home insulation, which the party saw as an alternative to Labour's pledge to cut value added tax on home heating fuel -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
